transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-11 16:30 UTC | Duration 48 min | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Connor (Redwood Solutions), Daniel Hsu (Neptune - Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (SRE), Marcus Lee (CFO), Olivia Park (Product)

Summary: high-level discovery on cost/unit economics for an LLM assistant that Neptune wants to ship across two products. Primary asks: understand per-token bill impact, how batching and KV/prefix caching will lower unit costs, and which hosting mode fits their budget and security posture.

00:00:05 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE working with you on this — quick round-robin?
00:00:12 Daniel: yeah daniel here, head of ml at neptune, we'll own model integration and quality.
00:00:16 Priya: priya kapoor, sre, i'll handle ops and network questions.
00:00:18 Marcus: marcus lee, cfo. short on time, will watch numbers.
00:00:22 Olivia: olivia, product manager.
00:00:25 Leah: leah martinez, solutions engineer at redwood, i'll go deep on batching and latency.

00:01:10 Samir: great, goal for today is to surface usage profile and constraints so we can put together a pilot that shows real per-token economics. two quick qs to start — what's your anticipated QPS and typical prompt lengths?
00:01:26 Daniel: for the search assist product, peak qps ~80 concurrent requests, average prompt + response ~800 tokens combined, but wide tail, sometimes 2k tokens for long form. For chat product it's lower concurrency, maybe 20 qps but hits higher context windows.
00:01:48 Leah: got it, and are those mostly read-only generations or do you have heavy embeddings and rerank workloads?
00:01:54 Daniel: mix — embeddings for indexing (batch jobs), reranking at inline latency, generation for assistant. Embedding volume is predictable but generation is spiky.

00:02:30 Marcus: budget question up front — we want predictable spend, target initial monthly opex around $30k for hosted costs, plus maybe dedicated reserved later if it proves out. How do we think hosted per-token maps to that?
00:02:45 Samir: good call. quick context: our hosted API pricing has per-token tiers and you can optimize with batching and prefix caching which materially reduces per-token bill when workloads have repeat prefixes or state. For your profile, rough back-of-envelope: at 800 avg tokens per request, naive hosted could be high, but with batching and a 30% cache hit you could reduce token bill by 20-40%. We'll model both.

00:03:30 Leah: to add: there are two levers — request-side batching (combine multiple requests into a batch to amortize compute) and KV/prefix caching which short-circuits repeated prefixes or system prompts. Also quantization/compact model variants reduce cost per token.

00:04:05 Priya: on dedicated vs hosted: any differences in token accounting? We care because procurement needs a capex/opex decision.
00:04:13 Leah: token accounting is consistent in the API, but dedicated gives you reserved capacity. That translates to predictable throughput and we can price as committed monthly capacity (e.g., per-GPU seat) rather than pure per-token. For heavy steady state, dedicated often lowers unit cost. For spiky workloads, hosted with burst makes sense.

00:05:00 Marcus: so if we lock into dedicated, do we still get caching and batching benefits?
00:05:06 Leah: yes — the runtime features (batching, kv-cache) are the same in dedicated and private. The difference is billing and isolation. Dedicated has committed billing and potential discounts; hosted is pay-as-you-go per token. Private on prem is license + infra.

00:06:10 Olivia: what's the easiest pilot to prove unit econ?
00:06:15 Samir: pilot approach: 2-week benchmark on a staging replay of your production traffic (or synthetic) where we run: baseline hosted runs, then enable batching, then enable KV caching and compact model variants. We'll produce a per-token breakdown and latency percentiles.

00:06:45 Daniel: can you run this against our data? privacy is a concern.
00:06:50 Leah: yes — we can either run on hosted with an IPSA (data delete policies) or do a dedicated evaluation where logs stay inside your tenancy. For sensitive content, we can recommend a private control plane or dedicated with VPC peering and KMS keys.

00:07:20 Marcus: our core ask: months 1-3 budget must be predictable, CFO wants scenarios: worst / expected / best case cost. Can you provide that?
00:07:30 Samir: absolutely — we'll produce a 3-scenario cost model. Need your traffic histogram and token distribution. Priya, can you share a sample day?
00:07:38 Priya: yes, i'll export a 72-hour sample and token counts per request.

00:08:10 Leah: small note — batching latency tradeoff. If you batch too aggressively you add tail latency. For 200–500ms SLOs you can batch windows of 10–20ms and still see good savings. For really tight 50–100ms SLOs dedicated with pre-warmed lanes or smaller models is better.

00:09:00 Daniel: our product needs 95th percentile <350ms for short responses (<200 tokens). Longer flows can be slower.
00:09:08 Leah: that's feasible. We'll show batch configs that keep p95 under 350ms while lowering token compute by 15–30% depending on traffic shape.

00:10:00 Marcus: what about egress/data residency? We need EU residency for EU customers. Is hosted available in eu-west?
00:10:08 Samir: yes, we have hosted regions in eu-west and us-east. For strict residency you'd pick dedicated in that region or private deployment. We also support customer-managed keys (KMS) and SOC 2 reports.

00:11:25 Olivia: curious about fallback — if the dedicated pool is saturated do you fallback to hosted?
00:11:30 Leah: we can configure routing policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to compatible hosted variants or smaller models. Routing is policy-driven and we can set cost thresholds.

00:12:20 Daniel: model variants — can you quantify cost delta between base model and 8-bit quantized variant?
00:12:27 Leah: roughly 30–50% compute reduction depending on model and latency. There's a small quality delta; we'll include evals. For many use cases quality is acceptable.

00:13:10 Priya: security doc ask — can you share SOC2, network diagrams, and an example private deployment topology?
00:13:16 Samir: yes, i'll attach our security pack.

00:14:00 Marcus: ok assume pilot runs and shows 25% token reduction with caching/batching, approx monthly hosted spend would be?
00:14:09 Samir: preliminary: with your numbers, naive hosted might be ~$45k/mo. With optimizations and 25% reduction we'd be ~$34k/mo. If you go dedicated and commit, unit cost could drop to ~$20–25k equivalent depending on reserved level. We'll run precise math in the spreadsheet.

00:15:00 Daniel: that's in line with what we need. Questions: how long to spin up a dedicated environment for a pilot?
00:15:06 Leah: typically 1–2 weeks for reserved capacity in our Dedicated offering; private on-prem can take longer (coordinated install and network). Hosted pilot is immediate.

00:16:00 Olivia: timeline wise, we'd like a pilot in May.
00:16:04 Samir: good, we'll aim to have the SOW + pricing by 2027-04-13 so you can sign and begin the week of 2027-05-04.

00:17:30 Marcus: procurement will need contract terms — any minimums?
00:17:36 Samir: hosted has no long minimums; dedicated has minimum commit periods (monthly/quarterly) — details in pricing doc. We'll include both contract templates.

00:18:50 Daniel: any gotchas on token counting? For example system prompts appended per turn — do you charge for that?
00:18:57 Leah: we count tokens per request and response; system prompts included. A common optimization is to use short encoded system prompts or reuse cached KV for repeated system context. We'll show you how to instrument and reduce those costs.

00:20:00 Priya: operational question — how do we monitor token usage and set alerts?
00:20:07 Samir: console exposes per-route token breakdown, per-model, cost per token over time, and alerting hooks. We'll share a sample dashboard.

00:22:00 Leah: quick technical note: for your embedding batch jobs you may want dedicated nodes for throughput, separate from real-time generation lanes. That helps cost and ensures tail latency for real-time is unaffected by heavy batch jobs.

00:25:00 Daniel: ok let's recap what you need from us to model costs precisely.
00:25:05 Samir: traffic histogram (72 hours), token distribution by endpoint, SLOs per endpoint, sample prompts, list of regions for residency, and quality thresholds for model variants.
00:25:20 Priya: i'll own traffic export.
00:25:22 Marcus: finance will expect three scenarios.
00:25:25 Samir: yes, we'll deliver worst/expected/best.

00:26:40 Olivia: last question, do you support per-route throttles to control spend?
00:26:45 Leah: yes, configured in Console: quotas, per-route rate limits, and graceful fallback to smaller models.

00:28:00 Samir: great, next steps we covered: send pricing, security pack, and schedule SE benchmark. Any other outstanding items?
00:28:10 Marcus: none.
00:28:12 Daniel: sounds good.

00:28:30 Samir: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the SOW and a proposed pilot schedule.

(Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions in names; some technical phrases transcribed imperfectly — e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes appears as 'K V cash' in earlier automated captions. Natural pauses and crosstalk present.)
